text: Mary Seacole was born in 1805 on the Caribbean Island of Jamaica, which was owned by the British at the time. Let’s go and meet her.

instruction.text: You’re talking to Mary Seacole about her childhood. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: My mother was a free Jamaican and my father was a Scottish ((++soldier dancer)), but he wasn’t around when I was growing up.
atoms.sound: My mother was a free jamaican and my father was a Scottish soldier, but he wasn’t around when I was growing up

atoms.b: What did you do when you were growing up?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-1st'>What did you do when you were growing up?</prosody>

atoms.b: I helped my mother run her hotel. She taught me lots about healing people with ((++herbal purple)) remedies. This was especially useful in 1850 when lots of people in Jamaica got cholera.
atoms.sound: I helped my mother run her hotel. She taught me lots about healing people with herbal remedies. This was especially useful in 1850 when lots of people in Jamaica got cholera.

hint.text: Cholera is a nasty infection mainly spread through dirty drinking water.
hint.label: Cholera

atoms.b: Who stayed in your mother’s hotel?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-1st'>Who stayed in your mother’s hotel?</prosody>

atoms.b: We had ((++many very_few)) sick and injured British soldiers come and stay with us, so I got to know them very well.
atoms.sound: We had many sick and injured British soldiers come and stay with us, so I got to know them very well.

atoms.a: Mary Seacole was born in Britain.
Mary Seacole grew up in Jamaica.
Mary Seacole’s mother owned a hotel in Jamaica.
Mary Seacole learnt about herbal remedies.
